 The Movie-Tie Book Cover of Kristin Hannah’s ‘The Nightingale’ Is Here—What Reese’s Book Club and Goodreads Fans Are Saying
 The WWII sister story that's moved millions of readers is finally headed to the big screen—and fans are already obsessed with the first look 
 By Maressa Brown 
 November 18, 2026 
 Comments 
 TOP STORIES 
 Lisa O'CONNOR/AFP via Getty Images; St. Martin's Griffin; Monica Schipper/Getty Images 
 Tap Here To Add Woman's World As A Trusted Source 
 Add as a preferred source on Google 
 Key Takeaways 
 Elle and Dakota Fanning star in 'The Nightingale' movie, arriving March 2027.
 Reese’s Book Club revealed the new 'Nightingale' tie-in cover, out January 12.
 Fans of Kristin Hannah can read 'The Women,' 'The Alice Network,' or 'Lilac Girls' next.
 For the first time ever, sisters Elle and Dakota Fanning will be joining forces in the film adaptation of bestselling author Kristin Hannah’s massive hit The Nightingale . The novel, which was published in 2015, tells the story of two sisters during World War II who each embark on their own path to survival, love, and freedom in German-occupied, war-torn France. Themes of resilience, women’s inner power, courage, and grace are woven throughout the beloved book. And to celebrate the film hitting theaters in March 2027, St. Martin’s Press has released a movie tie-in book cover that will be available in bookstores on January 12, and Reese’s Book Club recently shared a first look. Here’s what Reese’s Book Club and fans had to say and what fans of The Nightingale should read next.
 What to know about Reese’s Book Club post on the new cover
 In a November 16 Instagram post, Reese’s Book Club shared the new cover, writing, “Elle and Dakota Fanning are sharing the big screen for the first time ever in the movie adaptation of Kristin Hannah’s blockbuster book THE NIGHTINGALE, coming exclusively to theaters March 2027. Here’s a first look at the book tie-in cover, in bookstores January 12, and don’t miss the movie trailer this Thursday.”
 Fans quickly weighed in with their seal of approval. One noted, “OBSESSED WITH THIS COVER!! NEED IT NOW” while another wrote, “Loved, loved, loved this book! Can’t wait to see the movie.”
 Loading answers 
 Book lovers who have already fallen for Hannah’s storytelling feel fairly confident that the film adaptation is going to be as moving as the novel. One wrote, “I know the book wrecked me, but somehow I know these two will manage to END me with their portrayals. I can’t wait!!”
 View this post on Instagram 
 What Goodreads users love about ‘The Nightingale’
 The comments on Reese’s Book Club post about Hannah’s new cover echo a lot of the sentiments that Goodreads users have shared in their reviews of the book, which has an average rating of 4.65 from 2,439,064 ratings.
 “The women in particular, the sisters, were absolutely inspirational,” wrote one Goodreads user. “They showed incredible strength in this terrible time and I loved seeing how women contributed to the war. This was just a story that really resonated with me. It has a special place in my heart for it was truly, beautiful. If you like WWII historical fiction, or even if you don’t, I encourage you to try this book out. I know I’m going to be encouraging basically everyone I know to read it.”
 Another pointed out just how much of a tearjerker the novel is, writing, “The separations and the heartbreaks, the communication gaps and the unavoidable situations will break you. The ending is beautiful, yet it leaves you totally sobbing and broken. But your heart will have the acceptance and closure; the ending feels so wholesome. I have never cried so hard reading fiction in my entire life.”
 In a similar review, a Goodreads user wrote, “With tears still running down my cheeks, I’m writing this review. I’ve started this review several times and I don’t think I’ll be able to adequately put into words the power in which this novel has moved me. Truly a remarkable story that I, literally, beg everyone who loves historical fiction to read. I will be gushing about this novel for some time to come.”
 What fans of Kristin Hannah’s ‘The Nightingale’ will want to read next
 With a couple of months until the movie tie-in cover hits stores and several months until the film makes its way to theaters, fans of The Nightingale might be inspired to re-read the 2015 novel, to be sure. But if reading something new but similar sounds more appealing, here are a few options to consider:
 ‘The Women’ by Kristin Hannah
 Published in 2024, The Women is a coming-of-age story that celebrates women as heroes—specifically in the 1960s. Hannah tells the story of 21-year-old nursing student Frances “Frankie” McGrath who, in 1965, joins the Army Nurse Corps and goes to Vietnam—only to return home to a changed, divided country, angry protesters, and a country that wants to forget the war.
 ‘The Alice Network’ by Kate Quinn

 William Morrow 
 This historical novel, published in 2017, from national bestselling author Kate Quinn follows two women—a female spy named Eve recruited to the real-life Alice Network in France during World War I and an unconventional American socialite named Charlie searching for her cousin in 1947. A tale of strength and courage, Quinn’s story follows both women’s perspectives and ultimately brings the two together to uncover the truth of what happened to Charlie’s beloved cousin.
 ‘Lilac Girls: A Novel’ by Martha Hall Kelly
 This 2016 bestseller centers on the lives of three women who are set on a collision course when one of them, Kasia, is sent to Ravensbrück, the notorious Nazi concentration camp for women. From New York to Paris, Germany, and Poland, the moving story follows a group of memorable, courageous characters, two of whom are based on real women.
